# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants
data.title: Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.
data.title: Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches (use both cheap-mode slots)

# Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher creates panes for each work item it dispatches (intake, plan, audit, risk-effort), but panes stay open indefinitely until an operator closes them manually. There is no automatic pane lifecycle management — completed panes clutter the Dispatcher workspace and the dispatch log lacks pane-close status updates (intake complete, plan complete, audit passed/failed, or stuck). This work item adds automatic pane closing and enhanced logging for pane lifecycle events.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants the Dispatcher workspace to stay tidy; auto-closed panes reduce manual cleanup.
- **Producer** — wants a clear audit trail of pane outcomes in the dispatch log: which panes completed successfully, which are stuck, and which failed their audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The downtime worker logs every pane-close event to `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` with: ISO timestamp, work item ID, work item title, pane ID, dispatch kind (`plan`/`intake`/`audit`/`risk-effort`), and outcome (`closed-as-intake-complete`, `closed-as-plan-complete`, `audit-passed`, `audit-failed`, `requires-attention`).
- **AC2:** When a dispatched item's stage advances to `intake_complete` or `plan_complete`, the worker records the appropriate log entry and closes the associated pane (except for `kind === 'implement'` items).
- **AC3:** When a dispatched item is left in any other state (e.g. `in_review` without reaching a terminal state, or blocked by producer questions where `needsProducerReview === true`), the worker records a `requires-attention` log entry with a summary reason.
- **AC4:** When a dispatched item reaches `in_review` status (implementation completed), the worker records the event in the log.
- **AC5:** When an audit pane completes and the item's audit status is recorded (`auditedAt` set, audit passed or failed), the worker records the audit outcome in the log and closes the pane (audit panes are always auto-closed regardless of the `implement` exception).
- **AC6:** The `implement` kind is EXCLUDED from all auto-close logic — implement panes remain open until manually closed by the operator.
- **AC7:** All logging and pane-closing operations are fail-closed: a failed log write or pane-close attempt must never crash the worker or block subsequent dispatches.
- **AC8:** Full herdr + repo test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The existing `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` rolling JSONL format must be extended (not replaced); legacy entries remain valid.
- Pane closing must be safe — only panes that were spawned by the downtime worker for this specific work item should be closed.
- The worker must detect state changes without polling the worklog excessively; consider event-driven or reasonable polling cadence.
- The `implements` exception (AC6) is mandatory — no implement pane is ever auto-closed.

## Existing state

- Dispatch logging already exists via `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8): a bounded JSONL log recording dispatched items.
- The `AgentTracker` (`agent-tracker.ts`) already records work-item → pane-ID associations in `.worklog/agent-panes.json`.
- Panes are spawned via `send-to-pi.sh` with pane IDs that are captured and tracked.
- Panes currently stay open indefinitely — no auto-close mechanism exists.
- The worker polls `wl` commands periodically but does not track work-item state changes post-dispatch.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the dispatch log schema** to support pane-close and state-change entries with outcome reasons.
2. **Add a pane-lifecycle monitor** that tracks dispatched items after they are spawned, detecting when they reach terminal stages (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`) or when audits complete.
3. **Implement auto-close logic** that closes panes based on the detected outcome, with the `implement` exception.
4. **Log all lifecycle events** to the dispatch log with structured entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Core dispatch worker; add pane-lifecycle tracking and auto-close logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Extend log entry schema for pane-close outcomes.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — Already tracks pane IDs; may need extension for lifecycle callbacks.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — New tests for pane-close logic.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — *Log herdr downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling .worklog log)* — existing dispatch logging infrastructure.
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — *Work-item ↔ agent-pane association tracker* — `AgentTracker` that maps work items to pane IDs.
- **WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3** — *Remove client-side pane count cap* — panes now deliberately stay open until manually closed (context for why auto-close is new).
- **WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40** — *Dispatch-logs skill: generates 24h global dispatch report* — related observability.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should happen to panes for items that reach `in_review` but then revert to a different stage?" — Answer: Log the initial `in_review` arrival; if the pane is still open and the item changes again, log the new state. Only close panes at the specific terminal points defined in AC2–AC5. Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Does 'requires attention' apply to panes that are still actively running (agent in `working` state)?" — Answer: No — "requires attention" applies to panes where the agent session has ended (`done` state) but the work item has not reached a terminal stage (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`). Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Should the worker proactively close panes, or just log and signal?" — Answer: The worker should both log AND close the pane (except for implement). The pane close is an active action. Source: intake draft.
data.title: Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement

# Herdr mode-switch: raise default operator-idle threshold from 15 to 30 minutes

## Problem statement

The herdr plugin's activity-gated proxy mode-switch worker (WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9) drops
the llama-proxy to **cheap** mode once the operator has been idle. The default idle
window is currently 15 minutes
(`DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 900_000`), which proves too aggressive:
the operator stepped away only briefly and the proxy had already restarted onto the
cheap (local-first, 2-slot) pool, costing a mode-switch restart plus a later restart
back to fast.

The default should be **30 minutes**.

User story:

- *"As the operator, when I look away from the worklog for a few minutes, I do not
  want the proxy to drop to cheap mode; the default idle window should be 30 minutes
  so only a genuine absence triggers the switch."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` in `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` is `1_800_000` (30 minutes) and its doc comment states 30 minutes.
- [ ] The `clampModeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` doc comment references the 30-minute default (invalid/negative input falls back to the new default).
- [ ] The `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` field doc in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` states the new default (`1_800_000` / 30 min).
- [ ] The value is still overridable per-install via the existing `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` setting; the 60-second floor is **unchanged**.
- [ ] Unit tests assert the new default (`packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts`), and the clamp test still passes with the new default; `900_000`-based explicit-threshold fixtures in `mode-switch-worker.test.ts` remain valid (they pass the threshold explicitly).
- [ ] Documentation updated to state the new default: `packages/herdr/README.md` (settings section, `900000` = 15 minutes → `1800000` = 30 minutes) and `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` settings table.
- [ ] No behavior change other than the default value: per-slot operator gate, fast-switch-on-command, fail-closed semantics, single-flight/dedup, poll interval and its clamps are all untouched.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes.

> **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline and is excluded from this list.

## Constraints

- **Surgical change.** Only the default constant, the comments that state it, the tests that assert it, and the two docs that record it change. Do not refactor the worker.
- **The 60s floor stays.** `MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_MS` is unchanged; only the fallback/default moves.
- **No new setting.** This is a default change, not a new option; consumers still read the same `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` key.
- Build → test → commit discipline (vitest suite in `packages/herdr`).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts:79` — `export const DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 900_000;` with a `/ ** Default idle window before switching to cheap mode: 15 minutes. * /` comment (line 78) and `clampModeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` doc at line ~114 mentioning the "15-minute default".
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts:90,125,233-235` — field doc, `defaultSettings`, and load-time clamp fallback all route through the exported constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1429`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:6166` — consumers reading `s.modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs ?? DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (no change needed; they pick up the new default).
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — extensive explicit `idleThresholdMs: 900_000` fixtures; only the clamp assertion exercises the default symbolically.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts:167-186` — `'defaults to 900_000 ms (15 minutes)'` describes the default explicitly.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts:119` — `expect(DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS).toBe(900_000); // 15 minutes`.
- `packages/herdr/README.md:688-689`, `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md:57` — document the default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — default constant + comments
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — field doc comment
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts` — default assertion + title
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts` — default assertion
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — settings documentation
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` — settings table

## Related work

- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** – Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (cheap on operator idle, fast on operator command) — completed; the feature whose default this item retunes.
- **WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR** / **WL-0MT9FL9JO002JEAZ** – per-slot operator gate for the cheap switch — completed; the gate semantics that remain unchanged.
- **WL-0MT1EDYS0002CMUK** / **WL-0MT1EECPU0024Z7J** – mode-switch settings validation, clamps and integration — completed; the clamp contract preserved here.
- **WL-0MU6MXCZZ007ZXT9** – mode-switch flip-flop / leader election — open, unrelated to the threshold value.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the "default" the operator wants raised is the shipped default for fresh installs (and the fallback for invalid settings), not a forced override of an existing user's saved `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`. Existing installs that already persisted 900000 keep their value; only the default changes. Recorded because a forced migration was not requested.
- **Risk: low.** A constant change with test/doc updates; no control-flow change. The 60s floor and all fail-closed paths are untouched.
data.title: Herdr mode-switch: raise default operator-idle threshold from 15 to 30 minutes
